'''''Jania''''' is a [[genus]] of red macroalgae (or [[seaweed]]s) with hard, calcareous, branching skeletons in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Corallinaceae]]. 

== Taxonomy and Nomenclature ==
The genus name of ''Jania'' is derived from the Greek [[naiad|water nymph]] called [[Ianeira]] (or ''Janeria'').<ref>{{cite book |last=Burkhardt |first=Lotte |url=https://doi.org/10.3372/epolist2022 |title=Eine Enzyklopädie zu eponymischen Pflanzennamen |publisher=Botanic Garden and Botanical Museum, Freie Universität Berlin |year=2022 |isbn=978-3-946292-41-8 |location=Berlin |language=German |trans-title=Encyclopedia of eponymic plant names |format=pdf |doi=10.3372/epolist2022 |s2cid=246307410 |access-date=January 27, 2022}}</ref> It was first [[circumscription (taxonomy)|circumscribed]] by [[Jean Vincent Félix Lamouroux]] in 1812.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Lamouroux |first=J.V.F. |date=1812 |title=Extrait d'un mémoire sur la classification des Polypiers coralligènes non entièrement pierreux. |journal=Nouveaux Bulletin des Sciences, par la Société Philomathique de Paris |volume=3 |pages=181–188}}</ref> Based on a recent integrated taxonomic examination of the genus, and by extension its tribe Janieae, the members of ''Cheilosporum'' and ''Haliptilon'' have all been transferred under genus ''Jania''<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Kim |first1=J.H. |last2=Guiry |first2=M.D. |last3=Oak |first3=J.H. |last4=Choi |first4=D.S. |last5=Kang |first5=S.H. |last6=Chung |first6=H. |last7=Choi |first7=H.G. |date=2007 |title=Phylogenetic relationships within the tribe Janieae (Corallinales, Rhodophyta) based on molecular and morphological data: a reappraisal of Jania 1 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1529-8817.2007.00410.x |journal=Journal of Phycology |language=en |volume=43 |issue=6 |pages=1310–1319 |doi=10.1111/j.1529-8817.2007.00410.x|s2cid=84584053 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>''.'' As a result, there is currently around 55 confirmed species for this genus.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last1=Guiry |first1=M.D. |last2=Guiry |first2=G.M. |date=2023 |title=Jania J.V.Lamouroux, 1812 |url=https://www.algaebase.org/search/genus/detail/?genus_id=94 |access-date=19 January 2023 |website=AlgaeBase}}</ref>

== Morphology ==
''Jania'' is an articulated coralline algae characterized by having erect thalli with dichotomously-arranged branches composed of alternating segments of red or pink, calcified, cylindrical sections (intergeniculum) and white uncalcified sections (geniculum); that is attached to the substrate by small, stolon-like holdfasts.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Woelkerling |first1=W.J. |last2=Harvey |first2=A.S. |last3=de Reviers |first3=B. |date=2015 |title=Jania verrucosa and Jania crassa (Rhodophyta: Corallinaceae): Typification, nomenclature and taxonomic implications |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.12705/641.1 |journal=Taxon |language=en |volume=64 |issue=1 |pages=137–146 |doi=10.12705/641.1 |issn=|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":1" /> Intergenicula of this genus can be cylindrical, subcylindrical or compressed and smooth, winged or lobed.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />

== Distribution ==
''Jania'' species are well-distributed throughout the world.<ref name=":1" />

== Ecology ==
Members of the genus are found in sheltered reef habitats, often in crevices or other shaded areas.<ref name="MSIP">[http://species-identification.org/species.php?species_group=caribbean_diving_guide&id=479 Segmented algae (''Jania spp.'')] Marine Species Identification Portal. Retrieved 2011-12-31.</ref> They are also epilithic, epiphytic, and could form free-living clumps called articuliths.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tâmega |first1=Frederico T. S. |last2=Torrano-Silva |first2=Beatriz N. |last3=Oliveira |first3=Mariana Cabral |last4=Spotorno-Oliveira |first4=Paula |last5=Calazans |first5=Sávio H. |last6=Rosas-Alquicira |first6=Edgar Francisco |last7=Coutinho |first7=Ricardo |last8=Peña |first8=Viviana |date=2021-07-04 |title=Identification of 'articuliths' in a unique algal bed formation from Brazil and description of Jania cabista sp. nov. (Corallinales, Rhodophyta) |url=https://doi.org/10.1080/00318884.2021.1916279 |journal=Phycologia |volume=60 |issue=4 |pages=283–302 |doi=10.1080/00318884.2021.1916279 |s2cid=236296629 |issn=0031-8884|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Life history ==
Like most red seaweeds, ''Jania'' exhibit a triphasic life cycle wherein aside from the free-living haploid (gametophyte) and diploid (tetrasporophyte) generations, another diploid generation that is parasitic to the gametophyte, the carposporophyte. Tetrasporophyte (2N) generation would release four haploid spores (or tetraspores) that would later on develop into either the male and female gametophytes; moreover, the spermatium (N) produced by the spermatangia will be trapped by the trichogyne of the carpogonium (N) of the female gametophyte and later on fuse to form the zygote and subsequently develop into the carposporophyte (2N); lastly the carposporophyte will produce carpospores (2N) that will become the tetratsporophyte (2N).<ref name=":1" /> The unique structure involved in coralline reproduction is the presence of the conceptacle, a calcified depression wherein the tetrasporangia, spermatangia, and carposporangia are formed.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Johansen |first=H.W. |title=Reproduction of the Articulated Coralline Amphiroa Ephedraea |date=1968 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1529-8817.1968.tb04702.x |journal=Journal of Phycology |language=en |volume=4 |issue=4 |pages=319–328 |doi=10.1111/j.1529-8817.1968.tb04702.x |pmid=27068206 |s2cid=24515929 |issn=0022-3646|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Exploitation/harvesting/cultivation ==
There is no known cultivation technology for this genus.

== Chemical composition/natural products chemistry ==
Priming tomato seeds with ''Jania'' polysaccharides has shown to greatly improve the resistance of seedlings to soil-borne pathogens and consequently promote plant growth.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Righini |first1=Hillary |last2=Roberti |first2=Roberta |last3=Cetrullo |first3=Silvia |last4=Flamigni |first4=Flavio |last5=Quintana |first5=Antera Martel |last6=Francioso |first6=Ornella |last7=Panichi |first7=Veronica |last8=Cianchetta |first8=Stefano |last9=Galletti |first9=Stefania |date=2022 |title=Jania adhaerens Primes Tomato Seed against Soil-Borne Pathogens |journal=Horticulturae |language=en |volume=8 |issue=8 |pages=746 |doi=10.3390/horticulturae8080746 |issn=2311-7524|doi-access=free |hdl=11585/894150 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> 

== Utilization and management ==
Despite the potential use of ''Jania'' in agriculture and due to a lack of interest on this genus, this genus is not currently being commercially utilized.
